plays.fallback: If nobody has a plan, Brannagh does it anyway.
plays.title: They hide Ila at the Pilots' Hall
plays.why: The Court wants her; the Pilots' Hall is the safest roof in Pellmoor.
plays.readAloud: Brannagh looks at Ila over the sounding-line on her shoulder. 'Pilots' Hall has a loft nobody climbs. She'll have a hammock, a bell to ring if the gloves come, and a pilot on the stair.'
plays.response: Brannagh keeps Ila in the loft with a pilot on the stair, and the ferry-folk close ranks. Ila stays hidden until the party returns or the Court escalates. She argues, but accepts it if the party explains why; if they say 'don't worry', she stops speaking to that character.
plays.consequence: Ila is safe, and the Court's cart finds only an empty house.
plays.keywords: hide ila, pilots hall, safe house, protect ila, loft

plays.tells: A party that sold the Tongue to Quill or the Chancellor leaves Ila in her father's house.
plays.rules: No check.
plays.later: S4: Maudrin offers Ila's release for a favour (s04-exemption-releases-ila). S6: rescue alongside Tessa (s06-rescue-tessa-with-ila).
plays.fallback: If the party reacts in time, Brannagh's pilots delay the cart one day.
plays.title: Hushmen come for Ila at dawn
plays.why: The Tongue went to the Court and nobody sheltered her.
plays.readAloud: Grey wax on the Harrow door. Dorra Pell says it flatly: 'They came at first light. She went with her coat on and her head up.'
plays.response: Off-screen. Check session-zero Off-limits. Ila is taken by a Hushman Sergeant and two escorts and carried to Hallowmere, where she waits in the Hall of Tithes, a clean room with a bed. A courier from Brannagh's pilots can reach the cart before it leaves the Mere (s02-intercept-ila-cart applies on the road). Maudrin's offer will use her.
plays.consequence: Ila is under Court arrest.
plays.keywords: ila arrested, dawn, hushmen, taken, child arrested

plays.tells: The party has lied to Quill or named a villager to him in S1.
plays.rules: Influence DC 16 on Quill (Intelligence 11, Insight +5). If bribed, he takes more gold and complains less.
plays.later: S4: the Gate Clerk raises Persuasion DCs by 2 if Quill is Suspicious (s04-refuse-courtesy-memory).
plays.fallback: If the party fights him, run s01-attack-quill.
plays.title: Quill returns with a second Hushman
plays.why: The lie held, or the party named Mother Sallow to him; either way Quill's report is out.
plays.readAloud: Quill stands in the chapel door with a second Hushman behind him. 'Good morning,' he says. 'I was reviewing my notes and found a gap in my notes, and I thought you'd want to help me fill it.'
plays.response: He asks the coat question again, and if Mother Sallow's name was given, he asks for her ledger. He is polite; the second Hushman is not. He wants a reason to search. Persuasion DC 16 on Quill buys a week. Hold Person or Suggestion on Quill works but the Landing House reads the hum as a confession.
plays.consequence: The Court's pressure rises one notch.
plays.keywords: quill returns, second hushman, search, ledger, mother sallow

plays.tells: Hushmen move in the village, or the party asks who can be trusted.
plays.rules: No check. A hiding place gives Advantage on Stealth checks to hide a person or bundle on the Old Shore.
plays.later: S4 (siege): they shelter villagers. S6: Wren already trusts the party.
plays.fallback: If nobody asks, the households send a child with a loaf.
plays.title: The three households warn the party
plays.why: The party filled the quota, so three Bellwright-sympathising households owe them.
plays.readAloud: A boy slips a folded net-tag under your door: a thread tied in three knots. Downstairs, the woman whose quota you filled says only, 'Not tonight. They're at the chapel.'
plays.response: The households warn the party when Hushmen move, offer a hiding place for Ila or the Tongue, and later shelter villagers during a siege. They will not fight; they will lie. They do not ask for anything. Heroic Inspiration for a player who thanks them by name.
plays.consequence: The Old Shore has a back door.
plays.keywords: households, quota, warn, villagers owe, sympathisers

plays.tells: A player lifts a blade in the chapel, or waits for Eld on the Mere road.
plays.rules: Eld is a Priest Acolyte (CR 1/4) and can cast Silence once per day. A downed Eld can be knocked out instead of killed.
plays.later: S4: use an unnamed chaplain at the Assembly. S28: Mother Sallow knows who did it.
plays.fallback: If the player wavers, Eld offers the Tongue's page and a name of a child to warn.
plays.title: They kill Brother Eld
plays.why: Eld wrote down the names of children for the Court.
plays.readAloud: Eld does not run. 'I knew it would be someone,' he says. 'I'd like to ask only that you tell Mother Sallow I tried to keep the page.'
plays.response: Ask once: 'You mean to kill him?' A downed Eld can be bound. If he dies, the ferry-folk say nothing and the chapel stays shut. Say plainly that the only living witness to the Court's patrol entries is gone; the page and the forms still point at Quill and Hallowmere. No resurrection.
plays.consequence: Eld is dead. The Church notes it.
plays.keywords: kill eld, murder, chaplain, execute

plays.tells: A player asks whether the Heron can be stopped without a fight.
plays.rules: Influence DC 15 on Brannagh (Friendly if Ila vouches). Each day of delay adds one to clock_ferry. At 6 the Hall suspends a crossing.
plays.later: S3: s03-heron-sails runs the clock out if the Tongue is not recovered. Venn remembers.
plays.fallback: If Brannagh refuses, a Baldurian mate offers to 'lose' the Tongue overboard for 100 gp.
plays.title: Brannagh denies the Heron a pilot
plays.why: The Heron needs a pilot to leave the Mere, and Brannagh runs the Pilots' Hall.
plays.readAloud: Brannagh counts the tide out loud and shakes her head. 'No pilot leaves this hall for the Heron today. She'll sit till Venn's patience runs out.'
plays.response: Brannagh can delay the ship one day by refusing a pilot; a second day costs the Pilots' Hall a favour and Venn a fine. The delay buys the party time to board or buy back the Tongue. It also tells Venn exactly who is against him.
plays.consequence: The Heron's sailing is delayed by one day.
plays.keywords: delay ship, pilot, pilots hall, brannagh, heron

plays.tells: The party has not recovered the Tongue by the end of the third or fourth day.
plays.rules: No check. Three days after the sale, four if Brannagh delayed once.
plays.later: S4: Maudrin hears of it from Quill's replacement (s04-tell-where). S28: Ila never forgives the sale. Any time: any-heron-wrecks, or any-ossa-written-off if the table moves on.
plays.fallback: If the table is stunned, the Tidewarden says only: 'The Mere remembers what is taken from it.'
plays.title: The Gilded Heron sails with the Tongue
plays.why: Three or four days pass and the Tongue is still aboard.
plays.readAloud: The Heron slips her lines at the turn of the tide, a Pilots' Hall skiff ahead of her, and the last you see of her is a plum-coloured sail going into a wall of grey weather.
plays.response: Brannagh counts the days honestly. The Heron crosses the Seam in a day. The Tongue is beyond Corvane. Ossa cannot be rung until it returns. Tell the table plainly what this closes (the Concord) and what stays open (the Second Dawn). Offer the safety valve if the table wants it: the Heron wrecks in the Wall and the Mere returns the Tongue weeks later (any-heron-wrecks).
plays.consequence: Ossa's Tongue is gone through the Seam.
plays.keywords: heron sails, ship leaves, tongue gone, seam, abroad

plays.tells: A player asks what Venn wants for it, or counts out gold.
plays.rules: Influence DC 15 for the discount.
plays.later: S4: the Court hears of the sale from Quill but Venn is not exposed.
plays.fallback: If the party cannot pay, Brannagh offers to guarantee a loan.
plays.title: They buy the Tongue back from Venn
plays.why: They sold it in haste, or Ila found out.
plays.readAloud: Venn spreads his ringed hands. 'Twelve hundred, friend, or a heartkeep. You see I am a reasonable man. I paid six, I lose nothing, and I was so looking forward to Athkatla.'
plays.response: Venn sells it back for 1,200 gp or a heartkeep and enjoys the profit. He remains Friendly; the party now owes him nothing and he thinks well of them. Persuasion DC 15 brings it to 900 gp. A heartkeep is a defining memory, chosen by the player.
plays.consequence: The Tongue returns without a fight; Venn is a smiling creditor.
plays.keywords: buy back, venn, pay, heartkeep, 1200 gp, tongue

plays.tells: A player asks whether the Choir can be freed without the Cantor's help.
plays.rules: No check.
plays.later: S3: the verse is sung after Ossa rings (s03-sing-release).
plays.fallback: If the ledger is damaged, Ila hums the tune and Sallow supplies the words.
plays.title: Mother Sallow rebuilds the release verse
plays.why: They missed the Cantor's verse, but Sallow's ledger can rebuild it.
plays.readAloud: Mother Sallow reads from the restored ledger in a low voice. 'It was a funeral verse, once. They sang it in my grandmother's time. I lost it with the rest.'
plays.response: Sallow reads the verse from the ledger and teaches it. It takes an hour. The verse is the same as the Cantor's: four lines and a sincere commemoration.
plays.consequence: The party knows the release verse.
plays.keywords: verse, ledger, rebuild, mother sallow, choir release

briefs.pressure: The Coster ship Gilded Heron docks this morning and the Quays are loud with cargo. Tobias Quill's memory quota is short because Pellmoor pays its way in gold now; he reaches the Old Shore on the second evening with one guard (the first evening if Venn tips him off). Ila has not slept properly in six weeks. Strangers' Row, the Loud Quarter, is a short walk from the Quays: the Dawn Mission, the Brass Lantern and a forger's back room are all there. If the party does nothing, Quill finds the Tongue by the third day.
briefs.npcs: Ila Harrow, Mother Sallow, Hushman Tobias Quill, Dorra Pell, Pilot-Mistress Brannagh Wick, Reckoner Sela Maunt, Master Orsolo Venn, Sister Aurelie Dawnmantle, a Harper with a lute
checklist: Read 'Running this session (new DM guide)' near the end of this session's plan: every scene with read-aloud, each person's voice, the fights turn by turn, pacing and names
Decide how each character arrives: by ship through the Seam, by the Mere road, or already living in Pellmoor. Ask each player whether the character grew up under the Court (it matters at S5)
Have the Reckoning House slate ready: 1 keep = 1 gp 2 sp, motes 1 sp, heartkeeps by appraisal
Know Quill's one question: 'Where did the child's coat go?'
Prepare Mother Sallow's response hymn as a two-line call and answer you can sing or speak
Ask each player for one thing their character has lost; note it for the Toll and memory ledger
Written for four level-3 characters, who have subclasses and 2nd-level spells: have the any-l3 rulings plays open (Hold Person, Suggestion, Detect Thoughts, Locate Object, Misty Step)
Strangers' Row is where Aurelie, the Harpers and a forger are introduced: set aurelie, stormborn and writ from those plays
Make the Heart prop: something heavy wrapped in old cloth, with a phone on vibrate inside it (or hum one low note while Ila holds it)

briefs.pressure: The Night Song rises at dusk and the Old Shore hums back. The eastern-marsh ferry has been missing a week. Brother Hadrik Voss, a Kelemvorite from Strangers' Row, plans to 'lay the dead to rest' on the Memory Shore tonight. Quill writes his report to Hallowmere.
briefs.npcs: Mother Sallow, the Cantor (Ondra Sallow), the Tidewarden, Pilot-Mistress Brannagh Wick, Brother Hadrik Voss, Ila Harrow
checklist: Read 'Running this session (new DM guide)' near the end of this session's plan: every scene with read-aloud, each person's voice, the fights turn by turn, pacing and names
Mere Memory table (v5 Part 11.4) at hand; decide whether one failed save becomes Tam's last night (a clue)
2024 Suffocation and Frigid Water if anyone dives; the belfry top is about 40 feet down
Eel thefts: the player picks the lost minor memory; it returns after a long rest
Decide how the Cantor reacts to a true answer, and whether she teaches the release verse (only for a sincere memory of a dead person)
Check ila: if the raid took her, the Mere road cart is the rescue (s02-intercept-ila-cart)
S1 to S5 are level 3; the party reaches level 4 after the Hallowmere investigation (S6). Do not hand out levels in the Mere
Write each character's breath on a card in rounds: (1 + Constitution modifier) x 10, minimum 5

briefs.pressure: Brother Eld knows the page is missing and is frightened. Quill's report has reached Hallowmere. Master Venn sends a polite note offering to buy 'a humming relic'. The Chancellor's letter arrives at the end of the session whatever the party does.
briefs.endOn: What will you carry to Hallowmere?
briefs.npcs: Mother Sallow, Brother Eld, Ila Harrow, Master Orsolo Venn, Pilot-Mistress Brannagh Wick, the Cantor, the Tidewarden

Eld's papers: the missing page, the matching Court forms, and the patrol entry recording Tam's interrogation
Read the Ossa Toll aloud before any ringing: 'A memory of someone who has died. You choose it. If you say no, the bell does not ring.' Ila may not be the Ringer

Write the Chancellor's letter as a prop; it doubles as a writ of passage
Check ila: free, hidden, travelling or arrested decides which of the Ila plays show tonight
The party is still level 3 here; level 4 comes after S6

encounters.title: Quill's patrol
encounters.tactics: Quill walks the Old Shore with one Hushman; the other three wait with the keep-cart at the end of the lane and arrive at the start of round two (show their lantern coming). Two Hushmen hold the doorway with Pack Tactics while two flank through the net-racks and Quill backs toward witnesses. They target whoever holds the Tongue and use Arrest, not killing blows.
encounters.exit: Quill retreats toward the Landing House when his guard is Bloodied or a ferry-folk crowd gathers. He wants an arrest, never a death; a downed PC is bound, not killed.
encounters.scale: Written for four level-3 characters. Three PCs: drop two Hushmen. Five PCs or a party that opens with area spells or Hold Person on Quill: add a Hushman Sergeant who arrives in round two. The Landing House post (six Hushmen) comes only if the party chases Quill onto the Quays; telegraph boots on the boards a round early.

encounters.title: The night raid on the Harrow house
encounters.tactics: They search for the Tongue first and fight only if blocked. The sergeant watches the door and uses Command; two search; one waits by the boat.
encounters.exit: They withdraw when one drops or the Old Shore wakes (two rounds of noise). They never pursue onto the water.
encounters.scale: Written for four level-3 characters. Three PCs: no sergeant. Five PCs: add Quill outside, who flees at the first blow.

encounters.title: Memory-eels at the sandbank
encounters.tactics: They strike from below at anyone wading or swimming, and try to drag one character under. They ignore people sitting in boats for the first round.
encounters.exit: They flee when reduced to two, or when the dead ferryman's oar is raised. Sneaking past (DC 15 Stealth, half the group) avoids the fight.
encounters.scale: Written for four level-3 characters. The eels are the bait; the cold water and the drag-under are the pressure. Three PCs: four eels. Five PCs: eight. Don't chain this straight into the Drowned Singers: give a short rest on the sandbank.

encounters.title: Drowned Singers at the belfry
encounters.tactics: One Singer wails to frighten swimmers; the other grapples and pulls a diver down while the eels harry anyone left at the surface. The Cantor sings but does not join.
encounters.exit: It stops pursuit at the surface and treats Mother Sallow's response hymn as a ceasefire. Divers can always swim up.
encounters.scale: Written for four level-3 characters, but underwater: breath is the real clock, so it plays harder than its XP. Three PCs: one Singer. Five PCs: add a third Singer. Show their approach a round early. Paralysis stays removed from the Singer: a Paralyzed diver would drown.

encounters.title: The ferry-stair guard
encounters.tactics: Guards the ferry-stair against anyone the Choir marked as forgetful, or anyone who comes without the hymn or the Tidewarden.
encounters.exit: Singing the response hymn, returning the Tongue, or the Tidewarden's company ends it at once.
encounters.scale: Written for four level-3 characters (Moderate in practice on the stair, where only two can stand abreast). Brother Hadrik's forced blessing adds a fourth Singer. Three PCs: two Singers.

encounters.title: Boarding the Gilded Heron
encounters.tactics: The guards use Pack Tactics on deck; the mate, a Zhentarim hand Venn pays not to ask questions, goes for whoever holds the Tongue. The Baldurian crew stay out of it. Venn stays behind them and talks.
encounters.exit: Venn negotiates the moment a guard is Bloodied: the Tongue for safe passage off his ship and no complaint to the Court.
encounters.scale: Written for four level-3 characters. Add two guards if the party arrives with Hold Person and Invisibility ready. If the party sneaks aboard (DC 15 Stealth each), only one guard and the mate are on watch.

encounters.title: The Mere road cart
encounters.tactics: They keep the cart between themselves and the party, grapple anyone who reaches the tailboard, and shout for the next checkpoint. They do not drive the cart on while it is under attack.
encounters.exit: The Sergeant yields the cart when two Hushmen drop or the ferry-folk driver unhitches. A downed PC is bound and left at the ford.
encounters.scale: Written for four level-3 characters (Low). Three PCs: drop one Hushman. Five PCs: add a Hushman. Ila stays in the cart.
